rows.Name: sector88
rows.Notes:
We serve open models on the customer's own hardware, including air-gapped sites, and keep serving when the link to the outside goes down. Apertus (fully open, Apache-2.0, EU-AI-Act-aligned, 1000+ languages) is the kind of model those environments keep asking for. You provide the sovereign model. We provide a sovereign deployment path for it.

Today, our shipped runtime serves Apertus-8B on a single 24 GB GPU through vLLM with no changes, bf16, about 30 tok/s. The lighter GGUF route (6.2 GB, about 40-49 tok/s, CPU-capable) needs a one-dependency bump to our llama.cpp backend, which is queued. We have not tested the 70B.

rows.Name: LinkID – AI-Powered Persistent Link Resolution and Knowledge Preservation
rows.Notes:
LinkID is an AI-powered persistent identifier and link resolution platform developed by Link Genetic GmbH.

The solution addresses the global problem of link rot and content drift by creating persistent, machine-readable identifiers that remain valid even when the original web resources move, change, or disappear.

Apertus is integrated into the LinkID platform to provide intelligent semantic analysis and contextual understanding of web resources. By leveraging Apertus models, LinkID can:

• Analyze the content and meaning of referenced resources.
• Detect content drift and semantic changes over time.
• Support intelligent link repair and destination matching.
• Improve long-term preservation of digital knowledge.
• Assist in maintaining reference integrity in documents, websites, and knowledge bases.

The platform is currently being evaluated for applications in digital preservation, Wikimedia projects, scientific publications, enterprise document management, and public sector archives.

Technology:
- LinkID persistent identifier system
- Apertus AI integration
- AWS cloud infrastructure
- REST APIs
- PDF and web content processing

Audience:
Researchers, archivists, enterprises, government organizations, publishers, and knowledge management communities.

Project Status:
Prototype / Early-stage production deployment.

Open Source Components:
Selected components and specifications are published publicly to encourage interoperability and future standardization efforts.

rows.Name: Noemon
rows.Notes:
Builds AI that learns while it runs — applying its continual-learning technology to Apertus to extend context, cut costs, and enable private customization.

---

We are changing how AI scales by changing how it learns.

Backpropagation, the standard learning rule in AI, is upstream of many of the technology's limits: training cost, data requirements, brittle long-horizon behavior, centralized deployment, and the inability of systems to learn continually or improve through use.

We are replacing it.

We are building a paradigm based on local, plasticity-based, distributed learning: a path to training systems that also learn from experience during inference. We believe this capability is essential for robust long-horizon agents, personalized models, adaptable robotics, efficient inference, and the next regime of model scaling.

Changing the learning rule also changes the hardware frontier, as memory, bandwidth, power, architecture, and interconnects are shaped by learning at training and inference time.

Our team has been leading biologically plausible learning across neuroscience, machine learning, AI accelerators, and memory nanotechnology. We have previously founded unicorns, deployed deep technology in Antarctica and in space, built products used by millions, and sold to dozens of Fortune 500 companies.

We have been building in private.

rows.Name: bajour.ch / Promisly
rows.Notes:
At Bajour, Apertus is fully integrated into our daily production workflow. We are firmly convinced that ethically trained, open-source, and locally operated Large Language Models (LLMs) are essential for maintaining credibility and trust in modern journalism.

Specifically, we use a locally hosted Apertus instance for the daily processing and preparation of municipal news for our newsletter, the "Basel Briefing". Furthermore, we utilized Apertus to deeply analyze all cantonal council minutes from the past five years to track and verify political promises. This extensive data analysis recently resulted in a major exclusive story (Scoop: https://bajour.ch/a/klimawirkungsabschaetzung-basel-verzoegert-umsetzung-vom-klimacheck).

Bajour serves as a pilot medium within the We.Publish ecosystem. As is standard practice at We.Publish, successful pilot projects like ours are actively shared with their network of currently 15 independent media organizations. Through this We.Publish collaboration, the impact of our local setup is already scaling: right at this moment, the Apertus model is actively analyzing the city council minutes of Bern for our partner outlet hauptstadt.be.

Technical Details:
Model: 70B parameter model (Quantized: apertus-70b-Q4_K_M)
Implementation: Running on llama.cpp
Hardware: Local Nvidia Spark DGX with 128 GB unified GPU memory
Ecosystem: 100% Open Source
Interfaces: API and Web-UI. (Note: Our current Web-UI is access-restricted due to active production use. However, we are happy to set up a new demonstration instance upon request).

Links / References:
Bajour: https://bajour.ch/
We.Publish: https://wepublish.ch/
Contact: Samuel Hufschmid, samuel.hufschmid@bajour.ch, +41796069078

rows.Name: BetterCallMitch
rows.Notes:
Open Source Swiss Legal AI
https://github.com/fedec65/bettercallmitch

What it is
BetterCallMitch is the Swiss open-source alternative to Harvey and Legora — the leading commercial legal AI platforms. Built in collaboration with Mike OSS and powered by the BetterCallClaude.ch ecosystem, it delivers enterprise-grade legal AI capabilities to Swiss law firms without vendor lock-in, per-seat pricing, or enterprise contracts.
The project is owned and maintained by BetterCallClaude.ch, a Swiss non-profit association.

Core Features
FeatureDescriptionAI AssistantChat interface with document reading, verbatim citation, multi-step workflows, and end-to-end contract drafting. Supports Claude and Gemini via user-provided API keys. Comes pre-connected to 9 Swiss Legal MCPs.ProjectsMatter-scoped workspaces for uploading and managing legal documents (credit agreements, SPAs, leases, diligence packs) with persistent context across all conversations.Tabular ReviewSpreadsheet-style parallel extraction across hundreds of documents, with every cell verifiably cited back to a page and quote — no hallucinations.WorkflowsReusable prompt templates for standard legal tasks (CP checklists, credit agreement summaries, change-of-control reviews), shareable firm-wide.Ollama IntegrationLocal LLM support via Ollama for complete on-premises privacy — no API key required, models run on the firm's own infrastructure.

Why It Matters

Zero license cost — firms pay only model API costs, using their own Claude or Gemini keys
Self-hostable by design — documents never leave the firm's perimeter; full compliance with Swiss data residency requirements
Fully auditable — open prompts, open citation logic, open data flows — no black boxes
Extensible — forkable and customizable: add practice-specific workflows, DMS integrations, or custom citation engines


Swiss Legal MCP Integration
BetterCallMitch is deeply integrated with the BetterCallClaude.ch MCP infrastructure, providing direct access to Swiss legal sources including BGE search, Fedlex SPARQL, entscheidsuche, OnlineKommentar, and TAS jurisprudence — a unique advantage over generic international competitors.

Positioning

"All the features, no enterprise contract — built for Swiss lawyers."

BetterCallMitch addresses a clear market gap: Swiss law firms need AI tools that respect Swiss data sovereignty, understand the Swiss legal system, and don't come with the pricing and lock-in of US-headquartered platforms. It is the first serious open-source answer to Harvey and Legora in the Swiss market.
